chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq, from Sa'dan ibn Muslim, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Sweep your courtyards and do not resemble the Jews.'

key_terms.أَفْنِيَتَكُمْ: Your courtyards or open areas within a house compound

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of sweeping courtyards and not resembling the Jews in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) instructs believers to sweep their courtyards (*afniyah*), advising them not to imitate the Jews in this specific practice. Shia scholars, such as Al-Majlisi, note that this likely refers to a distinct Jewish custom of sweeping or cleaning their homes/courtyards in a particular manner or at a specific time, serving as a marker of communal identity and distinguishing Islamic etiquette from previous traditions.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Is’haq, from Sa’dan Bin Muslim, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Sweep your courtyards and do not resemble the Jews’.
en.sarwar: 5. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Ahmad ibn Ishaq from Sa‘dan ibn Muslim from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following:
“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘You must sweep the yard of your house and do not become similar to the Jews.’”
